title: dialog element and modal/non-modal behaviour
learningObjectives: Explain dialog element and modal/non-modal behaviour and choose an appropriate native HTML interaction.

understand.concept: The dialog element represents a dialog box. show() opens a non-modal dialog; showModal() opens a modal dialog in the top layer and makes the rest of the document inert. close() closes the dialog. A dialog can also be opened using the open attribute, but that is not the same as modal behaviour.
understand.whyItMatters: Modal dialogs change how users interact with the rest of the page. Use them only when the task requires focus, provide a clear close path, and avoid trapping users without a way to finish or dismiss the task.
understand.analogy: A modal dialog is like a focused conversation that temporarily pauses the surrounding room; a non-modal dialog leaves the room available.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual dialog, disclosure, and focus behaviour follows HTML and accessibility platform rules.

explain.narrative: The button opens the dialog modally. The form method=dialog button closes it using native dialog behaviour.

questions.prompt: Which method opens a dialog as a modal in the top layer?
questions.explanation: showModal() opens the dialog modally and makes the rest of the document inert.

questions.prompt: What should guide the choice between native and custom widgets?
options: Whether a native control meets the interaction requirement
Whether a custom widget looks more decorative
Whether ARIA can replace all HTML semantics
questions.answer: Whether a native control meets the interaction requirement
questions.explanation: Native controls are usually the safer choice unless the interaction genuinely requires custom behaviour.
